families.title: CubeDynamics
families.description: I build reproducible, cube-based workflows for observing environmental change through time.
families.question: How can multidimensional environmental data be analyzed reproducibly across space and time?

families.title: SpectralBridge
families.description: I connect field and Earth-observation data through cross-sensor calibration and spectral workflows.
families.question: How can measurements from different sensors be calibrated so field and Earth-observation data can be compared?

families.title: Wildfire growth & geometry
families.description: I connect questions about fire, spread, growth, structure, and environmental response across this line of work.
families.question: How do wildfire perimeter, spread, and growth change through time, and how can those dynamics be represented?

families.title: OASIS
families.description: I build working-group and hackathon infrastructure for collaborative environmental synthesis.
families.question: How can working groups and hackathons share reproducible infrastructure without rebuilding it for every collaboration?

families.title: Agentic infrastructure
families.description: I build containerized, standards-aware infrastructure for research agents and reproducible work.
families.question: How can research agents work in reproducible environments that respect FAIR and CARE principles?

families.title: ESIIL infrastructure
families.description: I contribute to the shared data, analytics, documentation, and group infrastructure behind ESIIL programs.
families.question: What shared data, analytics, and documentation infrastructure helps synthesis teams work together?

families.title: Open Life Science hackathon
families.description: I use these parallel group repositories to support hands-on open-science collaboration.
families.question: How can parallel group repositories support hands-on open-science collaboration?

families.title: Climate indices
families.description: I work on R packages and tools for accessing climate futures, drought, and landscape-response indices.
families.question: How can climate-futures, drought, and landscape-response indices be easier to access and use?

families.title: Ecological sampling
families.description: I use sampling design and simulation to explore spatial, phylogenetic, and ecological questions.
families.question: How does sampling design change what we can learn across geographic, phylogenetic, and ecological spaces?

methodology.activity_score: 5 × active days (30d) + 3 × commits (0–30d) + 2 × commits (31–60d) + commits (61–90d) + 6 × releases (90d)
methodology.active_repository: I call a repository active when GitHub returns at least one public commit authored by me in the trailing 90 days.
methodology.observed_contributor: I use ‘observed contributor’ for a non-bot identity returned by GitHub's contributors endpoint for a repository in this dataset.

limitations: My repository set combines public repository discovery, recent authored-commit search, and project names I curated; it may not include every repository in my history.
I use GitHub's contribution calendar, which can include commits, issues, pull requests, and reviews; I do not present it as my lifetime commit count.
My recent commit counts include only public commits GitHub attributes to the ttuff author identity, and I bound search results to 90 days.
I use contributor lists to describe GitHub repository contributors, not necessarily my direct collaborators or complete project teams.
I use current default-branch language bytes as context; they do not measure my effort or proficiency.
When CI, release, license, or package data is missing, I treat it as unavailable in the GitHub surface I queried—not as proof that none exists elsewhere.
